prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your needs (location in Dallas, roof type, budget, whether it’s an insurance claim, etc.). A quick way for me to give specific recommendations is to know your ZIP code and whether you need a residential or commercial replacement.

Meanwhile, here’s a practical checklist that tells you what to look for so you can find the best roofer for your job:

What to confirm before hiring
- Proper licensing and insurance: Ask for license numbers and verify them with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (if applicable). Verify general liability and workers’ comp insurance and ask for certificates showing the policy dates.
- Manufacturer certification: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, etc., indicate higher training and warranties.
- Local experience: A company that has worked in Dallas neighborhoods will know local codes and permitting.
- Written estimate and scope of work: Get at least three detailed bids that list materials, brand/models, number of squares, underlayment, ventilation, removal and disposal, start/finish dates, cleanup, and payment schedule.
- Written warranty: Distinguish between manufacturer shingle warranty and contractor workmanship warranty; get both in writing.
- References and reviews: Ask for local references and check Google, Yelp, and the BBB for recent reviews and complaints.
- Permits and inspections: The company should pull required permits and arrange final inspections if applicable.
- Payment terms: Avoid large up-front cash payments; typical deposits are reasonable (e.g., 10–30%), final payment on completion and inspection.

Questions to ask every roofer
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide certificates?
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand I want?
- Who will supervise the crew? Will subcontractors be used?
- What is included in the estimate (felt, underlayment, ice & water shield, flashing, vents, ridge vent, drip edge, tear-off)?
- What warranties do you provide (length and coverage)?
- Will you obtain permits and handle inspections?
- How will you protect landscaping and clean up after the job?

Red flags
- No written contract or estimate
- Pressure to sign immediately or pay all cash up front
- Excessively low bids with vague scope
- No local references or many unresolved BBB complaints
- Unwillingness to provide proof of insurance or license

If you want, give me your ZIP code and whether the job is residential or commercial (and if it’s an insurance claim). I’ll look up top-rated, well-reviewed Dallas roofers and return a short vetted list (3–5) with notes on certifications, strengths, and what to ask each one.
